shared_context.medical_history: diabetes; bodybuilder using anabolic steroids; 2 packs/day smoking since age 25; 2-7 alcoholic drinks/day; 17 lb weight loss over the last month

snippets.output: Given the progressive right arm symptoms over a few weeks, decreased sensation, 2/5 strength, dull aching and burning right arm pain, and the 55-year-old male’s medical history, the most likely diagnosis is brachial plexopathy, a condition in which the brachial plexus, a network of nerves that supplies the arm, is damaged. Brachial plexopathy can cause arm weakness, numbness, and pain.
snippets.pattern_notes: Final diagnosis conclusion merged with definition and supporting features (weakness, numbness, pain) of brachial plexopathy.

snippets.output: Apical lung tumor would typically present with symptoms such as cough, hemoptysis, and weight loss.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single atom, standalone fact about apical lung tumor presentation.

snippets.output: Cerebral infarction would typically present with sudden onset of symptoms and can cause hemiparesis, aphasia, and visual field defects; these findings are not consistent with the presentation of this 55-year-old male with right arm weakness developing over a few weeks.
snippets.pattern_notes: Conclusion (not consistent with presentation) supported by typical features of cerebral infarction.

snippets.output: Scalenus anticus syndrome is caused by compression of the brachial plexus by the anterior scalene muscle and typically causes arm pain and weakness that are relieved by changes in head and neck position. In this 55-year-old male with right arm pain and weakness, the symptoms are unchanged with head and neck position, arguing against scalenus anticus syndrome.
snippets.pattern_notes: Definition and typical relieving feature combined with conclusion that scalenus anticus is unlikely because symptoms are not position-relieved.

snippets.output: Subclavian steal syndrome is a condition in which the subclavian artery is narrowed or blocked, leading to decreased blood flow to the arm, and it would typically present with other symptoms such as arm fatigue and Raynaud's phenomenon.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of properties of subclavian steal syndrome: pathophysiology plus typical symptoms.
